two_commit_disclosure.what_happened: the CW3 writer process completed the whole round, but its stage list still named only src/security, src/effect and src/assurance even though the round's admitted write-set and its test roots already included src/observability. The observability repair therefore landed on disk, ran (102 tests) and was reported in the round receipt, but was NOT committed by that process.
two_commit_disclosure.the_tell: the observability test count moved (97 -> 102) while the commit delta contained no observability path - a count that moves without a corresponding artifact is the same class of signal as a repair whose collected count does not move
two_commit_disclosure.repair: commit 89287e2 carries the three subsystem repairs; commit 316f7923 carries the observability repair (src/observability/redaction.py, src/observability/tests/test_redaction.py, src/observability/tests/test_adversarial.py), staged and committed explicitly. The harness stage list was corrected permanently so the round can no longer stage a subset of its own admitted write-set.
two_commit_disclosure.effect_on_verification: the intermediate commit 89287e2 is NOT the subject of any checker run; the FINAL subject 316f7923 contains all four subsystem repairs and is the only subject handed to round 4
